subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit soft-steer mode or command that interrupts or pauses active generation/tool execution and resumes with injected user input, or should steer remain boundary-based?
rationale: The choice affects queue-mode semantics, Codex/native runtime behavior, channel-visible timing, partial transcript state, and compatibility with existing steer/followup/interrupt modes.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume behavior with tests for active generation, tool calls, partial output, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current steer semantics as the supported default and use related issues only to ensure messages reach the existing model-boundary policy.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Make default steer use the stronger interrupt/resume lifecycle only after explicit upgrade proof and channel/runtime compatibility coverage.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume behavior with tests for active generation, tool calls, partial output, backend rejection, and fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest routing candidate from the active-run steering replacement and adjacent lifecycle history.
